newsitem.title: USA: Northeastern U.S. spot power slips on mild weather.
newsitem.headline: Northeastern U.S. spot power slips on mild weather.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices for Tuesday delivery in northeastern U.S. slipped in light activity Monday amid an outlook for mild weather in the region this week.
Day-ahead power prices in the Northeast moved lower, albeit not as much as other regions around the country, market sources said.
Possible return of two key nuclear generating units to full production this week also weighed bearishly on prices. marketers and traders said.

The 1,137 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Nine Mile Point nuclear power facility restarted over the weekend, and its operator Niagara Mohawk Power Corp said the Scriba, N.Y., unit was scheduled to resume operation this week.
Market sources said Nine Mile Point 2 could achieve full output as early as Wednesday.

The 832 MW James A Fitzpatrick nuclear plant, also in Scriba, N.Y., continued toward full output after being shut December 15 to repair a leak in the electrical hydraulic control system. The station was operating at 62 percent early Monday, according to today's Nuclear Regulatory Commission's plant status report.

The weather forecast continued to push natural gas prices lower. Swing natgas prices at the New York City gate collapsed to a $4.28-$4.30 per million British thermal unit (mmBtu) range from Friday's $4.90-$5.00.
Christmas Eve temperatures in most of the Northeast were predicted to peak in 40s Fahrenheit degree range and bottom in the 20s.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices for Tuesday delivery in the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) dropped to $20.00-$22.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) from Friday's $24.00-$25.00 range for Monday.
Off-peak, non-firm power for next-day delivery in western NYPP stayed in a notational range $15.00-$16.00.
In eastern NYPP, Tuesday's peak, non-firm power was valued at $26.50-$28.00/MWh, down from Friday's $28.00-$30.00.
Eastern NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Tuesday edged down to $18.00-$19.00 from Friday's range of $19.00-$20.00 for Monday.

In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Tuesday at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border were valued in a $30.00-$33.00 range, compared with a quote of $35.00 Friday for Monday.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Tuesday delivery to the NU border was assessed at $20.00-$22.00, compared with Friday's $21.00-$22.00.
